paper_metadata.title: The effects of ruthenium on the phase stability of fourth generation Ni-base single crystal superalloys

evidence.quote: The formation of topologically close-packed (TCP) phases in nickel-base single crystal superalloys causes considerable degradation of the mechanical properties.
A third generation nickel-base single crystal superalloy TMS-121, which contains 5 wt.% Re, was used as the base alloy.
By adding 2 and 2.5 wt.% Ru to TMS-121, two other superalloys were cast. They have been named TMS-138 and TMS-138+, respectively
